newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pope's nuncio to move to bohemian Berlin district.
newsitem.headline: Pope's nuncio to move to bohemian Berlin district.

text.p: The Roman Catholic Church said on Wednesday the Vatican will move its German mission to the edge of Berlin's bohemian Kreuzberg district, notorious since the 1960s for its squatters, drug dealers and anarchist riots.
Kreuzberg, also the de facto capital of Germany's marijuana legalisation movement, will border the future headquarters of the Pope's German nuncio.

"Along with the diplomatic representatives of many countries, the Holy See will come to Berlin at the time of the move of the federal government and parliament in 1999," the press office of the Archbishop of Berlin said in a statement.

Last month, Kreuzberg was the focus of the wildest of the annual Berlin May Day riots, during which leftist radicals rampaged through the district's streets, breaking windows and throwing stones at police into the night.
Most recently, Kreuzberg streets filled with the Carnival of Cultures, a Rio-style parade with thumping drums, bare-breasted dancers and free-flowing revelry.
The Archbishop's spokesman said a planning board including church representatives and local politicians would meet soon to discuss designs for the new building.
